Hi Aditya,

Thanks for sending the DPA draft yesterday. Before we route to legal, there are three items Fintegral needs clarified / tightened so we can sign quickly:

1) Retention windows — we need confirmation that customer data in active indexes will be deleted within 30 days of request, and that backups are not used for any processing and will be deleted within 180 days.
2) Backup/DR carve-out — your previous draft allowed unspecified retention for disaster recovery. We need a clear upper bound and an accessibility/authorization model (who can restore, under what process).
3) Subprocessors and transfer — please confirm the current subprocessor list and commit to 30 days' notice before onboarding any new subprocessor that will process EU personal data.

We'd prefer not to redline heavily; if you can confirm acceptance in writing and send the e-sign envelope (DocuSign), procurement will finalize sign-off.

Laura — thanks for the clear list. High level responses below; copying Monica from Legal and Priyom from Sales for alignment.

1) Active data deletion: we confirm a 30-day window to complete deletion of active customer data on request. We will provide a deletion confirmation report.

2) Backups: Redwood will retain immutable, encrypted backups for disaster recovery only. Proposed upper bound: 180 days from snapshot date. Backups are logically isolated from serving systems and cannot be used for model training or other processing. Access to restore requires approval from our Security team and the customer's designated admin(s).

3) Subprocessors & transfers: current documented subprocessors list attached; Redwood will provide 30 days' notice prior to onboarding any subprocessor that will handle EU personal data. For EU-US transfers we propose SCCs (standard contractual clauses) and appropriate safeguards.

Team — drafting suggested clauses below (will push into the redline PDF):

- Active Data Deletion: "Customer data in active production systems will be deleted within thirty (30) days of Customer's verified deletion request. Redwood will provide a deletion attestation that includes scope and timestamp."

- Backup/DR Exception: "Redwood may retain encrypted, immutable backups created as part of routine disaster recovery operations for a period not to exceed one hundred eighty (180) days from the date of the backup snapshot. Such backups will be retained solely for the purpose of restoring Customer data in the event of data loss or system outage, will not be used for any other processing (including model training), and will be accessible only to personnel specifically authorized by Redwood's Security organization and the Customer's named admin(s). Restoration from backup requires documented approval from Redwood Security and the Customer's security contact. Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to purge backup copies earlier when feasible."

- Subprocessor notice: "Redwood will maintain an up-to-date list of subprocessors and will provide Customer with at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice before engaging any new subprocessor that processes Customer personal data. Customer may reasonably object to a new subprocessor during such notice period; if objection is not resolved within thirty (30) days, Redwood may terminate the applicable services for that Customer."

Note: procurement may still push for 90 days or shorter, but 180 days with the strong access controls is a common compromise that balances DR needs with customer expectations. I've attached the redline and the current subprocessor inventory.
